pairs.fullEnglish: These are the generations of Noach. Noach was a righteous man, whole in his generations; Noach walked in the fear of יְיָ.
Noach fathered three sons: Shem, Cham, and Yefes.
The earth became corrupt before יְיָ, and the earth became filled with robbery.
יְיָ saw the earth, and behold, it had become corrupt, for all flesh—each one—had corrupted its way upon the earth.
יְיָ said to Noach: The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth has become filled with robbery because of their evil deeds; and behold, I am going to destroy them together with the earth.
Make yourself an ark of cedar wood. You shall make the ark with compartments, and you shall coat it inside and outside with pitch.
This is how you shall make it: the ark's length shall be three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
And I—behold, I am bringing the flood, water upon the earth, to destroy from beneath the heavens all flesh in which there is the spirit of life. Everything on the earth shall die.
I shall establish My covenant with you, and you shall enter the ark: you, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
From everything living, from all flesh, you shall bring two of each into the ark, to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.

From the birds according to their kinds, from the livestock according to its kind, and from every creeping creature of the earth according to its kinds, two of each shall come to you to be kept alive.
And you, take for yourself from every food that is eaten, and gather it to yourself; it shall be for you and for them to eat.
Noach did so; according to everything that יְיָ commanded him, so he did.
יְיָ said to Noach: Enter the ark, you and every person of your household, for I have seen you to be righteous before Me in this generation.
From every clean kind of livestock you shall take for yourself seven by seven, male and female; and from the livestock that (is) not clean, two, male and female.
Also from the birds of the heavens, seven by seven, male and female, to keep offspring alive upon the face of all the earth.

For at the appointed time, in seven more days, I shall bring rain down upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I shall wipe away from the face of the earth every existing creature that I have made.
Noach did according to everything that יְיָ commanded him.
Noach was six hundred years old, and the flood was water upon the earth.
Noach entered the ark, and his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives with him, because of the waters of the flood.
From the clean livestock, from the livestock that is not clean, from the birds, and everything that creeps upon the earth,
two by two they came to Noach, into the ark, male and female, as יְיָ commanded Noach.
It happened at the appointed time of seven days that the waters of the flood were upon the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noach's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.
Rain came down upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noach entered the ark, with Shem, Cham, and Yefes, Noach's sons, and Noach's wife and his sons' three wives with them.

They, and every wild animal according to its kind, and all livestock according to its kind, and every creeping creature that creeps upon the earth according to its kinds, and every bird according to its kinds—every bird, everything that flies.
They entered the ark with Noach, two by two, from all flesh in which there is the spirit of life.
Those entering, male and female of all flesh, entered as יְיָ commanded him; and יְיָ protected him (by His Word).
The flood was upon the earth for forty days; the waters increased and lifted the ark, and it was raised above the earth.
The waters grew strong and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved upon the face of the waters.
The waters grew exceedingly, exceedingly strong upon the earth, and all the high mountains beneath the whole heavens were covered.
The waters rose strongly fifteen cubits above, and the mountains were covered.
All flesh that moved upon the earth died: among the birds, among the livestock, among the wild animals, and among every creeping creature that creeps upon the earth, and all humankind.

He wiped away every existing creature upon the face of the earth, from humankind to livestock, to creeping creatures, and to the birds of the heavens; they were wiped away from the earth. Only Noach and those with him in the ark remained.
The waters remained strong upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
יְיָ remembered Noach, and every wild animal and all the livestock with him in the ark. יְיָ caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters became still.
The springs of the deep and the windows of the heavens were closed, and the rain from the heavens was held back.
The waters receded from upon the earth, continually going and receding; and the waters diminished at the end of one hundred and fifty days.
The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of קַרְדּוּ.
The waters continued to diminish until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first of the month, the tops of the mountains became visible.
At the end of forty days, Noach opened the window of the ark that he had made.
He sent out the raven, and it went out, going out and returning, until the waters dried up from upon the earth.
He sent the dove out from with him, to see whether the waters had lessened from upon the face of the earth.

The dove found no resting place for the sole of its foot and returned to him, to the ark, for water was upon the face of all the earth. He stretched out his hand, took it, and brought it in to himself, into the ark.
He waited another seven days, and again sent the dove out from the ark.
He waited another seven days and sent out the dove, and it did not return to him again.

In the six hundred and first year, in the first month, on the first of the month, the waters had dried away from upon the earth. Noach removed the covering of the ark and saw, and behold, the face of the earth had dried.
In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
יְיָ spoke with Noach, saying:
Go out from the ark: you, your wife, your sons, and your sons' wives with you.

Bring out with you every living creature that is with you, of all flesh, among the birds, among the livestock, and among every creeping creature that creeps upon the earth; they shall reproduce on the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon the earth.
Noach went out, and his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives with him.
Every wild animal, every creeping creature, every bird, everything that creeps upon the earth, went out from the ark according to their families.
Noach built an altar before יְיָ, took from every clean kind of livestock and from every clean kind of bird, and offered up burnt offerings upon the altar.

יְיָ accepted his offering with favor, and יְיָ said by His Word: I shall not again curse the earth because of the sins of humankind, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from its youth; and I shall not again wipe out everything living as I have done.
Throughout all the remaining days of the earth, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease.
יְיָ blessed Noach and his sons and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.
Every moving creature that is alive shall be yours to eat; like the green vegetation, I have given you everything.
But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat.

But your blood, for your lives, I shall demand; from the hand of every wild animal I shall demand it, and from the hand of a human being—from the hand of a man who sheds his brother's blood—I shall demand the human life.
And you, be fruitful and multiply; reproduce on the earth and multiply upon it.
יְיָ said to Noach and to his sons with him, saying:
And I—behold, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your children after you,

and with every living soul that is with you, among the birds, among the livestock, and among every wild animal of the earth that is with you, from all that went out of the ark, to every wild animal of the earth.
I shall establish My covenant with you: all flesh shall never again be destroyed by the waters of a flood, and there shall never again be a flood to destroy the earth.
יְיָ said: This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between My Word and you and every living soul that is with you, for everlasting generations.
I have placed My bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between My Word and the earth.
It shall be, when I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bow shall appear in the cloud.
I shall remember My covenant that is between My Word and you and every living soul in all flesh, and the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The bow shall be in the cloud, and I shall see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between the Word of יְיָ and every living soul in all flesh upon the earth.
יְיָ said to Noach: This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between My Word and all flesh upon the earth.
Noach's sons who went out from the ark were Shem, Cham, and Yefes; and Cham was the father of כְּנָעַן.
These three were Noach's sons, and from these the inhabitants of the whole earth spread out.
Noach, a man who worked the soil, began and planted a vineyard.
He drank of the wine and became drunk, and he became uncovered within his tent.
Cham, the father of כְּנָעַן, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers in the street.

Shem and Yefes took the garment and placed it upon the shoulders of both of them. They walked backward and covered their father's nakedness; their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father's nakedness.
Noach awoke from his wine and knew what his younger son had done to him.
He said: Cursed is כְּנָעַן; a slave serving slaves shall he be to his brothers.
He said: Blessed is יְיָ, the God of Shem, and let כְּנָעַן be a slave to them.
May יְיָ grant enlargement to Yefes, and may He cause His Presence to dwell in Shem's tent; and let כְּנָעַן be a slave to them.
Noach lived three hundred and fifty years after the flood.
All the days of Noach were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
These are the generations of Noach's sons, Shem, Cham, and Yefes; sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Yefes were גּוֹמֶר, מָגוֹג, מָדַי, יָוָן, תוּבָל, מֶשֶׁךְ, and תִירָס.
The sons of גּוֹמֶר were אַשְׁכְּנַז, רִיפַת, and תוֹגַרְמָה.
The sons of יָוָן were אֶלִישָׁה, תַרְשִׁישׁ, כִּתִּים, and דֹדָנִים.
From these the island regions of the nations were divided in their lands, each according to his language, according to their families, among their nations.
The sons of Cham were כּוּשׁ, מִצְרַיִם, פּוּט, and כְּנָעַן.
The sons of כּוּשׁ were סְבָא, חֲוִילָה, סַבְתָּה, רַעְמָה, and סַבְתְּכָא; and the sons of רַעְמָה were שְׁבָא and דְדָן.
כּוּשׁ fathered נִמְרֹד; he began to be a mighty, powerful man on the earth.
He was a mighty, powerful man before יְיָ; therefore it is said: Like נִמְרֹד, a mighty, powerful man before יְיָ.
The beginning of his kingdom was בָּבֶל, אֶרֶךְ, אַכַּד, and כַלְנֵה, in the land of בָבֶל.
And רֶסֶן, between נִינְוֵה and כָּלַח; that is the great city.
מִצְרָאֵי (alternative reading: מִצְרַיִם) fathered לוּדָאֵי, עֲנָמָאֵי, לְהָבָאֵי, and נַפְתּוּחָאֵי.
And פַּתְרוּסָאֵי, and כַּסְלוּחָאֵי—from there the פְּלִשְׁתָּאֵי came forth—and קַפּוּטְקָאֵי.
כְּנַעַן fathered צִידוֹן, his firstborn, and חֵת,
and יְבוּסָאֵי, אֱמוֹרָאֵי, and גִּרְגָּשָׁאֵי,
and חִוָּאֵי, עַרְקָאֵי, and אַנְתּוֹסָאֵי,
and אַרְוָדָאֵי, צְמָרָאֵי, and חֲמָתָאֵי; afterward the families of the כְּנַעֲנָאֵי spread out.
The boundary of the כְּנַעֲנָאֵי was from צִידוֹן, reaching toward גְרָר as far as עַזָּה, reaching toward סְדוֹם, עֲמוֹרָה, אַדְמָה, and צְבוֹיִם, as far as לָשַׁע.
These are Cham's sons, according to their families, according to their languages, in their lands, among their nations.
To Shem also, the father of all the children of עֵבֶר, the brother of the elder Yefes, children were born.
The sons of Shem were עֵילָם, אַשּׁוּר, אַרְפַּכְשַׁד, לוּד, and אֲרָם.
The sons of אֲרָם were עוּץ, חוּל, גֶתֶר, and מַשׁ.
אַרְפַּכְשַׁד fathered שָׁלַח, and שֶׁלַח fathered עֵבֶר.
Two sons were born to עֵבֶר. The name of one was פֶּלֶג, for in his days the earth was divided; and his brother's name was יָקְטָן.
יָקְטָן fathered אַלְמוֹדָד, שָׁלֶף, חֲצַרְמָוֶת, and יָרַח,
and הֲדוֹרָם, אוּזָל, and דִּקְלָה,
and עוֹבָל, אֲבִימָאֵל, and שְׁבָא,
and אוֹפִר, חֲוִילָה, and יוֹבָב; all these were the sons of יָקְטָן.
Their dwelling place was from מֵשָׁא, reaching toward סְפַר, the mountain of the east.
These are Shem's sons, according to their families, according to their languages, according to their lands, among their nations.
These are the families of Noach's sons, according to their generations, among their nations; and from these the nations were divided upon the earth after the flood.
The whole earth had one language and one speech.
When they journeyed at first, they found a plain in the land of בָבֶל and settled there.

They said: Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower, with its top reaching to the height of the heavens; and let us make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered upon the face of all the earth.
יְיָ revealed Himself to exact retribution for the deeds of the city and the tower that human beings had built.
יְיָ said: Behold, they are one people, and they all have one language; and this is what they have begun to do. Now nothing that they have planned to do will be withheld from them.
Come, let Us reveal Ourselves and confuse their language there, so that each person (each man) will not understand the language of his fellow.
יְיָ scattered them from there upon the face of all the earth, and they ceased building (variant: they were prevented from building) the city.
Therefore he called its name בָּבֶל, for there יְיָ confused the language of the whole earth, and from there יְיָ scattered them upon the face of all the earth.
These are the generations of Shem. Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered אַרְפַּכְשָׁד, two years after the flood.
Shem lived five hundred years after he fathered אַרְפַּכְשָׁד, and he fathered sons and daughters.
אַרְפַּכְשַׁד lived thirty-five years and fathered שָׁלַח.
אַרְפַּכְשַׁד lived four hundred and three years after he fathered שֶׁלַח, and he fathered sons and daughters.
שֶׁלַח lived thirty years and fathered עֵבֶר.
שֶׁלַח lived four hundred and three years after he fathered עֵבֶר, and he fathered sons and daughters.
עֵבֶר lived thirty-four years and fathered פָּלֶג.
עֵבֶר lived four hundred and thirty years after he fathered פֶּלֶג, and he fathered sons and daughters.
פֶלֶג lived thirty years and fathered רְעוּ.
פֶלֶג lived two hundred and nine years after he fathered רְעוּ, and he fathered sons and daughters.
רְעוּ lived thirty-two years and fathered שְׂרוּג.
רְעוּ lived two hundred and seven years after he fathered שְׂרוּג, and he fathered sons and daughters.
שְׂרוּג lived thirty years and fathered נָחוֹר.
שְׂרוּג lived two hundred years after he fathered נָחוֹר, and he fathered sons and daughters.
נָחוֹר lived twenty-nine years and fathered תָּרַח.
נָחוֹר lived one hundred and nineteen years after he fathered תֶּרַח, and he fathered sons and daughters.
תֶרַח lived seventy years and fathered Avram, נָחוֹר, and הָרָן.
These are the generations of תֶּרַח: תֶּרַח fathered Avram, נָחוֹר, and הָרָן; and הָרָן fathered Lot.
Avram and נָחוֹר took wives for themselves. The name of Avram's wife was שָׂרָי, and the name of נָחוֹר's wife was מִלְכָּה, the daughter of הָרָן, the father of מִלְכָּה and the father of יִסְכָּה.
שָׂרַי was barren; she had no child.
The days of תֶרַח were two hundred and five years, and תֶּרַח died in חָרָן.
You shall make a light for the ark, and you shall finish it to a cubit at the top. You shall put the ark's doorway in its side; you shall make it with lower, second, and third compartments.
All those on dry land in whose nostrils was the breath—the spirit of life—died.

The fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every wild animal of the earth and upon every bird of the heavens, upon everything that the earth brings forth as creeping creatures and upon all the fish of the sea; they shall be delivered into your hands.
The blood of whoever sheds human blood shall be shed on the testimony of witnesses, by order of the judges; for He made humankind in the image of יְיָ.
They said to one another: Come, let us cast bricks and burn them in fire (blazing fire). The brick served them as stone, and bitumen served them as mortar.
Behold, My servant, the Messiah, will prosper; he will be exalted, grow great, and become exceedingly strong.

so he will scatter many peoples. Kings will fall silent because of him and place their hands upon their mouths, for they have seen what had not been told to them, and have understood what they had not heard.
Who has believed this good news of ours? And the might of the powerful arm of יְיָ—upon whom has it now been revealed?
Because they hated knowledge and did not desire the fear of God,
they did not desire my counsel and disregarded all my rebuke.
They will eat of the fruit of their ways and be filled with their own counsels.
For the turning away of the simple will kill them, and the error of fools will destroy them.
Then he will pray concerning our sins, and our iniquities will be forgiven on his account. But we were considered crushed, stricken from before יְיָ, and afflicted.

He will build the sanctuary that was profaned through our sins and handed over through our iniquities. Through his teaching, peace will increase upon us; and when we heed his words, our sins will be forgiven us.
All of us were scattered like sheep; each went into exile in the direction of his own way. From before יְיָ there was a will to forgive the sins of all of us on his account.

He prays and is answered; before he opens his mouth, it is accepted. He will hand over the mighty ones of the peoples like a lamb for slaughter, and like a ewe silent before its shearers. There is no one opposing him who opens his mouth to speak a word.
Whoever listens to me will dwell in hope and be at rest from the disturbance of evil.
My son, if you receive my words and keep my commandments hidden with you,
and incline your ear to wisdom and turn your heart toward understanding,
and if you call for discernment and raise your voice for understanding,

From before יְיָ there was a will to refine and purify the remnant of His people, to cleanse their souls of sins. They will see the kingship of their Messiah; sons and daughters will increase, they will lengthen their days, and those who practice the Torah of יְיָ will prosper through His favor.

He will rescue their souls from the subjugation of the peoples. They will see punishment upon their enemies and be satisfied with the plunder of their kings. Through his wisdom he will vindicate the righteous, in order to bring many into subjection to Torah, and he will pray concerning their sins.

Therefore I shall allot him the plunder of many peoples, and he will divide the possessions of mighty cities as spoil, because he handed over his life to death and brought rebels into subjection to Torah. He will pray concerning many sins, and the rebels will be forgiven on his account.
and seek it like silver, desiring it like stored-up treasures,
then you will understand the fear of God and find knowledge from before God.
For God gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
He stores up splendor for the upright and aids those who walk without blemish,
to guard the paths of judgment; and He will guard the paths of the righteous.

Sing praise, יְרוּשְׁלֶם, who was like a barren woman who had not given birth. Pour forth praise and rejoice, who was like a woman who had not conceived. For the children of desolate יְרוּשְׁלֶם will be more numerous than the children of the inhabited city, says יְיָ.
For you will grow strong toward the south and toward the north. Your children will inherit peoples and settle desolate towns.

Do not fear, for you will not be ashamed; do not be humbled, for you will not be disgraced. For you will forget the shame of your youth, and you will no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
For your Master, Who made you—יְיָ צְבָאוֹת is His name—and your Redeemer, the Holy One of יִשְׂרָאֵל, will be called the God of all the earth.
Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and the uprightness of every good path.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.
Counsel will watch over you; understanding will guard you,
so that you may escape from the evil way and from the man who speaks crooked things—
those who abandon upright paths and walk in paths of darkness,
who rejoice to do evil and exult in the perverseness of wickedness,
For a brief hour I put you far away; with great compassion I shall bring your exiles near.
In a little wrath I withdrew the face of My Divine Presence from you for a brief time; with everlasting kindness that does not cease I shall have compassion upon you, says your Redeemer, יְיָ.

For the mountains will pass away and the hills will break apart, but My goodness will not depart from you, יְרוּשְׁלֵם, and My covenant of peace will not be put far away, says יְיָ, Who is to have compassion upon you.
whose ways are crooked and whose paths are twisted—
None who enter return in peace, nor do they attain the paths of life.
Just as the house of יִשְׂרָאֵל waited for him for many days, while their appearance was darkened among the peoples and their radiance was darkened more than that of other human beings—

The righteous one will grow great before Him—behold, like shoots that flourish and like a tree sending its roots beside streams of water. So will holy offspring increase in a land that had need of him. His appearance will not be an ordinary appearance, nor his dread the dread of a common person; the radiance of holiness will be his radiance, so that everyone who sees him will gaze upon him.

qualifications.he: לֵיהּ הוא כינוי זכר יחיד, ונשמר באנגלית בכינוי המושא 'him', בלי להוסיף שם למי שהארץ היתה צריכה לו. אין בכך זיהוי עצמאי של הכינוי מעבר לתיאור הצדיק ותולדת הקודש שבקטע.
qualifications.en: לֵיהּ is masculine singular and is retained as 'him,' without inserting a name for the one the land needed. This does not independently identify the pronoun beyond the passage's description of the righteous one and holy offspring.

pairs.fullEnglish: Then the glory of all kingdoms will become an object of contempt and will cease. They will be weak and suffering—behold, like a person in pain and subject to illnesses—just as, when the face of the Divine Presence was withdrawn from us, we were despised and not esteemed.

From sufferings and punishment he will bring our exiles near. Who can recount the wonders that will be done for us in his days? For he will remove the rule of the peoples from the land of יִשְׂרָאֵל; the sins that my people committed will reach them.

qualifications.he: המשפט מזכיר את החטאים שחטא עמי ואומר שיגיעו אליהם. האנגלית משמרת את החטאים כנושא ואת הכינוי 'אליהם', בלי להוסיף שם למקבלי ההגעה ובלי להחליף את החטאים בנושא מפורש אחר. אין כאן קביעה עצמאית מי מצוין בכינוי או פירוט של אופן הגמול.
qualifications.en: The clause names the sins my people committed and says that they will reach them. The English retains sins as the subject and 'them' as a pronoun, without adding a named recipient or replacing sins with a different explicit subject. It does not independently identify that pronoun or specify how retribution occurs.
qualifications.anchor: חוֹבִין דְחָבוּ עַמִי עַד לְוַתְהוֹן יִמְטוֹ

pairs.fullEnglish: He will hand over the wicked to Gehinom, and he will hand over the wealthy in possessions who committed violence to a death of destruction, so that those who commit sin will not endure and will not speak deceit with their mouths.
Enlarge the place of your dwelling-house; do not hold back inhabitants from the towns of your land. Increase the people of your camps and strengthen your rulers.

qualifications.he: הצירוף מתורגם כאיסור למנוע יושבים מערי הארץ: אין להותיר את הערים בלי יושביהן באמצעות מניעת היישוב. התרגום שומר את יחס 'מן' ואת היושבים כמושא המניעה; אין זו הוראה להוציא תושבים מן הערים או תיאור של מסלול הגירה מסוים.
qualifications.en: The clause is rendered as not withholding inhabitants from the towns of the land. It retains the 'from' relation and inhabitants as what must not be withheld; it is not an order to expel residents or a description of a particular migration route.

pairs.fullEnglish: For the Divine Presence of יְיָ has encountered you—you who were like a woman forsaken and distressed in spirit, and like a wife of youth who was put far away—says your God.

This is before Me like the days of Noach: I swore by My Word that the waters of the flood which were in the days of Noach would not again pass over the earth. So I have sworn by My Word that My anger will not rest upon you and that I will not rebuke you.
so that you may escape from a woman who is an outsider, from the foreign woman whose words are sweet,

qualifications.he: חִילוֹנִיתָא נמסר כלשון זרות או הימצאות מחוץ למסגרת, ואחריו נוּכְרֵיתָא, אשה זרה. אין כאן שימוש במונח המודרני 'חילונית' או קביעה שכל אשה מארץ אחרת מתוארת כך. הפסוקים הבאים מתארים את האשה המסוימת ואת שכחת ברית אלהים.
qualifications.en: חִילוֹנִיתָא is rendered in its broad outsider sense, followed by נוּכְרֵיתָא, 'foreign woman.' This does not assign the modern category 'secular' or describe every woman from another land. The following verses characterize the particular woman and her forgetting God's covenant.

pairs.fullEnglish: For her house is in the depth of death, and the course of her path is toward the mighty ones.

qualifications.he: 'אל הגיבורים' משמר את שם העצם שבמקור בתוך דימוי עומק המוות. האנגלית אינה מוסיפה שמות או מזהה את הגיבורים עם קבוצה היסטורית מסוימת; היא גם אינה מחליפה את שם העצם בכינוי אחר מן הפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: 'Toward the mighty ones' retains the source noun within the imagery of the depth of death. The English supplies no names or particular historical group and does not replace the noun with a different designation from the Hebrew verse.

pairs.fullEnglish: O esteemed city enduring insult, of which the peoples say, “She will not be comforted”—behold, I shall set your paving stones in antimony and complete you with precious stones.

qualifications.he: חֲשִׁיבָתָא מציין כאן עיר חשובה ומוערכת, ואילו מְקַבְּלָא עוּלְבַּן מתאר את העלבון שהיא סובלת. אלה שני תיאורים של אותה עיר, ולא האמירה שהיא ׳נחשבת כמקבלת עלבון׳. תיאור העמים שאינה עתידה להינחם עומד כנגד הבטחת הבנייה הבאה אחריו.
qualifications.en: חֲשִׁיבָתָא describes the city as esteemed, while מְקַבְּלָא עוּלְבַּן describes the insult she endures. These are two descriptions of the same city, not the assertion that she is 'regarded as receiving insult'. The peoples' claim that she will not be comforted is set against the rebuilding promise that follows.

qualifications.he: 'באנטימון' מוסר כאן את שם חומר הצביעה המסורתי בתוך דימוי שיבוץ האבנים. אין בכך קביעה של הרכב כימי מדויק או של שיטת בנייה היסטורית.
qualifications.en: 'In antimony' names the traditional pigment material within the stone-setting image. It does not specify an exact chemical composition or a historical construction method.

pairs.fullEnglish: Haran died in the presence of Terah his father, in the land of his birth, in the fire of the Chaldeans.

qualifications.he: אוּרָא מתורגמת כאן לפי משמעותה הארמית הרגילה: אש; הדל״ת מצרפת אליה את כַסְדָּאֵי, הכשדים. התרגום אינו מחליף את הצירוף בשם המקום שבפסוק העברי ואינו מאמץ פירוש של בקעה. נאמר שהָרָן מת באש, אך לא נוספו כבשן, זהות המשליך לאש או סיבת המוות הקשורה באביו. פירוש רש״י על העברית מביא סיפור של מוות באש וגם פירוש אחר למילה העברית; אין הוא עד לנוסח ארמי אחר.
qualifications.en: אוּרָא is translated here in its ordinary Aramaic sense, fire; the following genitive relates it to the Chaldeans, כַסְדָּאֵי. The translation does not replace the expression with the Hebrew verse's place-name or adopt the interpretation valley. The rendering says that Haran died in the fire, but adds no furnace, person who cast him into it, or causal role for his father. Rashi's discussion of the Hebrew supplies both a death-by-fire narrative and another interpretation of the Hebrew word; it is not evidence for a different Aramaic text.

pairs.fullEnglish: From that land (alternative reading: from that counsel) the Assyrian went out and built נִינְוֵה, רְחֹבֹת of the city (alternative reading: the city's broad places), and כָּלַח.

qualifications.he: הקריאה הראשית מתארת יציאה מן הארץ ההיא. בחלופה עֵיצָה, ׳מן העצה ההיא׳ פירושו פרישה מן העצה או התוכנית, ולא יציאה ממקום ששמו עצה. פרטי העצה אינם מפורשים כאן. אֲתוּרָאָה הוא היוצא והבונה בשתי הקריאות. בהמשך נשמר ההבדל בין רְחֹבֹת שבקריאה הראשית לבין רְחוֹבֵי קַרְתָּא שבחלופה, ׳רחובות העיר׳.
qualifications.en: The main reading describes departure from that land. In the alternative עֵיצָה, 'from that counsel' means withdrawal from that counsel or plan, not departure from a place named Counsel. The plan's contents are not specified here. The Assyrian is the departing builder in both readings. The later main reading רְחֹבֹת remains distinct from alternative רְחוֹבֵי קַרְתָּא, 'the city's broad places.'

pairs.fullEnglish: When your terror comes unawares, and your ruin comes like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you—

qualifications.he: בְּשִׁלְיָא הוא כאן צירוף תוארי הפועל מן השקט, המתאר ביאה בלי התרעה, בהפתעה. אין זו קביעה שהבהלה עצמה שקטה או שהסביבה נשארת שקטה בזמן בואה. דימוי הסערה נאמר בנפרד בצלע הבאה, כְּעַלְעוֹלָא.
qualifications.en: בְּשִׁלְיָא is used here as an adverbial expression based on quietness, describing arrival unawares, without warning. It does not assert that the terror itself is quiet or that the surroundings remain quiet while it arrives. The whirlwind comparison is separately expressed in the next clause, כְּעַלְעוֹלָא.

pairs.fullEnglish: who abandons the upbringing of her youth and forgets the covenant of God.

qualifications.he: מַרְבִּיתָא נמסרת כשם עצם המציין גידול וחינוך, והצירוף דְטַלְיוּתָהָא קושר אותו לימי נעוריה של האישה. החינוך הוא הדבר שהיא עוזבת; לא נוספו מגדל אישי, בעל או אב. זהו תרגום של המילה הארמית ושל צירופה, ולא החלפתה בכינוי האישי שבפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: מַרְבִּיתָא is rendered as the noun for nurture or upbringing, with דְטַלְיוּתָהָא relating it to the woman's youth. The upbringing is what she abandons; no individual nurturer, husband, or father is supplied. This translates the Aramaic noun and its attachment rather than replacing them with the Hebrew verse's personal designation.

pairs.fullEnglish: תֶּרַח took Avram his son, Lot the son of הָרָן, his son's son, and שָׂרַי his daughter-in-law, the wife of Avram his son; and they went out with them from the fire of the Chaldeans to go to the land of כְנָעַן. They came as far as חָרָן and settled there.

qualifications.he: אוּרָא נמסרת כאש, כמו בְּאוּרָא שבפסוק 11:28; כאן מִן מציינת את נקודת היציאה, ולא שינוי במשמעות השם. התרגום אומר שיצאו מן האש, אך אינו מוסיף הצלה, בריחה מכבשן או סיפור על המשתתפים באירוע כזה. מסגרת המסע אינה מחייבת להחליף את השם הארמי בשם מקום מן העברית. נשמרים ׳יצאו עמהם׳, היעד המבוקש כְנָעַן וההגעה והישיבה בפועל בחָרָן; דברי רש״י על זהות היוצאים אינם בירור של אוּרָא.
qualifications.en: אוּרָא is rendered as fire, as in בְּאוּרָא at 11:28; here the preposition marks the point of departure, not a change in the noun's sense. The translation says that they went out from the fire, but adds no rescue, escape from a furnace, or narrative assigning participants to such an event. The journey frame does not require replacing the Aramaic noun with a place-name from the Hebrew. 'They went out with them', the intended destination כְנָעַן, and the actual arrival and settlement at חָרָן remain distinct. Rashi's explanation of the travelers does not gloss אוּרָא.

pairs.fullEnglish: The dove came to him at evening time, and behold, an olive leaf, broken off, was resting in its mouth; and Noach knew that the waters had lessened from upon the earth.

qualifications.he: תְּבִיר מתאר את העלה כשבור או תלוש. נָחִית מתאר כאן את מצב העלה המונח בפי היונה: במילון יאסטרוב מובא הפסוק במשמעות של מונח, ונָחִית מצוין במפורש כנוסח דפוס וינה. התרגום אינו מתאר את ירידת העלה, אינו מציין מי הניחו בפי היונה ואינו קובע מסלול שבו הגיע לשם. צורת הזכר מתייחסת לעלה ואינה קובעת שהיונה זכר.
qualifications.en: תְּבִיר describes the leaf as broken or plucked off. נָחִית here describes the leaf resting in the dove's mouth: Jastrow cites this verse under the sense of being placed or resting and expressly records נָחִית as the Vienna edition's reading. The rendering does not describe the leaf's descent, identify anyone who put it in the dove's mouth, or specify its route there. The masculine form refers to the leaf and does not establish a male dove.

dayTitle.en: Noach and the corruption of the earth

explanation.he: נח מתואר כצדיק וכשלם בדורותיו, והליכתו מתוארת כהליכה ביראת יי. כנגדו מתוארת הארץ כמלאה חטיפה מחמת מעשים רעים, והוא מצטווה להכין תיבה בעלת מדורים ולצפותה בכופר.
explanation.en: Noach is described as righteous and whole in his generations, and his conduct is described as walking in the fear of יְיָ. In contrast, the earth is filled with robbery because of evil deeds, and he is commanded to prepare an ark with compartments and coat it with pitch.

dayTitle.en: The ark's dimensions and the promise of the covenant

explanation.he: הציווי מפרט את מידות התיבה, את האור, את הפתח ואת מדוריה. לצד ההודעה על המבול ועל מות החיים בארץ ניתנת לנח הבטחת ברית, והוא מצטווה להיכנס עם בני משפחתו.
explanation.en: The command specifies the ark's dimensions, its light, its doorway, and its compartments. Alongside the announcement of the flood and the death of life on the earth, Noach receives a promise of a covenant and is told to enter with his family.

dayTitle.en: Preserving life and entering the ark

explanation.he: נח מצטווה להביא לתיבה זכר ונקבה מן החיים ולאסוף מזון לו ולהם. התרגום מעיד שעשה ככל אשר נצטווה, ולאחר מכן בא הציווי להיכנס עם כל אנשי ביתו מפני צדקתו בדורו.
explanation.en: Noach is commanded to bring male and female living creatures into the ark and to gather food for himself and for them. The translation states that he did everything he was commanded, after which he is told to enter with every member of his household because of his righteousness in his generation.

dayTitle.en: The final preparations for the flood

explanation.he: הציווי מבדיל בין הבהמה הטהורה לשאינה טהורה ומורה גם על לקיחת עופות לשם קיום זרע. לאחר ההודעה על זמן ירידת הגשם מתוארים עשיית נח וכניסתו עם משפחתו לתיבה מפני מי המבול.
explanation.en: The command distinguishes clean livestock from livestock that is not clean and also directs the taking of birds to preserve offspring. Following the announcement of the time when the rain will descend, the reading describes Noach's obedience and his entry into the ark with his family because of the floodwaters.

dayTitle.en: The creatures arrive and the waters begin

explanation.he: החיים נכנסים לתיבה שניים שניים, זכר ונקבה, כפי שנצטווה נח. הקריאה מציינת את מועד בוא מי המבול, את בקיעת מעיינות התהום ופתיחת חלונות השמים, ואת ירידת הגשם במשך ארבעים יום וארבעים לילה.
explanation.en: The living creatures enter the ark two by two, male and female, as Noach was commanded. The reading gives the time when the floodwaters arrived, describes the bursting of the springs of the deep and the opening of the windows of the heavens, and records forty days and forty nights of descending rain.

dayTitle.en: The strength of the waters and the drying of the earth

explanation.he: הקריאה מתארת את כניסת החיים לתיבה, את התגברות המים ואת אובדן החיים שמחוץ לה. לאחר שיי זוכר את נח ואת החיים שעמו, המים נחים ופוחתים; שילוח העורב והיונה והסרת מכסה התיבה מלווים את תיאור יבוש הארץ.
explanation.en: The reading describes the creatures' entry into the ark, the increasing strength of the waters, and the loss of life outside it. After יְיָ remembers Noach and the creatures with him, the waters become still and diminish; the sending of the raven and dove and the removal of the ark's covering accompany the account of the earth drying.

dayTitle.he: היציאה מן התיבה, הברית ותולדות העמים
dayTitle.en: Leaving the ark, the covenant, and the generations of the nations

explanation.he: נח ובני ביתו יוצאים מן התיבה, ונח מקריב קרבנות המתקבלים ברצון; בהמשך נמסרים ציוויים והברית שסימנה הקשת, והתרגום מדגיש את מימרו של יי. הקריאה מספרת על נח ובניו, מפרטת את משפחות העמים ואת פיזור בוני העיר והמגדל לאחר התגלות לשם פירעון, וממשיכה בתולדות שם עד משפחת תרח ובואה לחרן.
explanation.en: Noach and his household leave the ark, and Noach offers sacrifices that are accepted with favor; commands and the covenant whose sign is the bow follow, with the translation emphasizing the Word of יְיָ. The reading recounts events involving Noach and his sons, sets out the families of the nations and the scattering of the builders of the city and tower following a revelation for retribution, and continues the generations of Shem through תֶּרַח's family and its arrival in חָרָן.

dayTitle.en: The servant identified as Messiah and the hope of the house of Israel

explanation.he: התרגום מכנה את העבד ״משיחא״ ומתאר הצלחה, גדלות והשתקת מלכים. בית ישראל נזכר במפורש כמי שסבל מראֶה חשוך בין העמים וציפה לו. הדימויים הבאים מתארים צמיחה, קדושה והיפוך מעמד המלכויות.
explanation.en: The Targum explicitly calls the servant the Messiah and describes success, greatness, and the silencing of kings. The house of Israel is named as having waited for him while its appearance was darkened among the peoples. The ensuing images speak of growth, holiness, and the reversal of the kingdoms’ glory.

dayTitle.en: Listening, receiving the words, and directing the heart

explanation.he: ההקשבה לחכמה מתוארת כמביאה תקווה ומנוחה מבהלת הרעה. הפנייה לבן מדגישה קבלת דברים, הצפנת מצוות, הטיית האוזן והפניית הלב להבנה. הקטע מסתיים בקריאה לבינה ובהרמת הקול למענה.
explanation.en: Listening to wisdom is described in terms of hope and rest from the disturbance of evil. The address to the son emphasizes receiving words, storing commandments, inclining the ear, and turning the heart toward understanding. It ends with calling for discernment and raising one’s voice for understanding.

dayTitle.en: Jerusalem’s praise and the enlargement of her settlement

explanation.he: ירושלים נמשלת לאשה שלא ילדה ונקראת לשבח ולשמחה על ריבוי הבנים. ההרחבה מתוארת בלשון יישוב, מחנות ושלטון, ובמפורש לכיוון דרום וצפון. הבושה וההרחקה ניצבות מול תיאור הגאולה ופגישת השכינה.
explanation.en: Jerusalem is compared to a woman who had not given birth and is called to praise and joy over the increase of children. Expansion is described through settlement, camps, and rule, explicitly toward the south and north. Shame and distance are set beside redemption and the encounter with the Divine Presence.

dayTitle.he: הבנת הדרך ושמירת הלב מפני הרע
dayTitle.en: Understanding the way and guarding the heart from evil

explanation.he: כניסת החכמה ללב והנעימות שבדעת מלוות בשמירה של עצה ובינה. התוצאה המתוארת היא הימלטות מדרך רעה ומדיבור עקום. בהמשך נזכרים העוזבים דרכים ישרות ושמחים בעשיית הרע.
explanation.en: Wisdom entering the heart and the pleasantness of knowledge are joined with the guarding work of counsel and understanding. The stated result is escape from an evil way and crooked speech. The following clauses describe those who abandon upright paths and rejoice in doing evil.

dayTitle.en: Everlasting compassion and the covenant of peace

explanation.he: ההרחקה הקצרה עומדת מול רחמים מרובים וקירוב הגלויות. ההבטחה נמסרת בלשון מימר ה׳ ונקשרת לימי נח ולמי המבול. טוב ה׳ וברית שלומו מובחנים מן ההרים והגבעות העוברים, ובסיום בא תיאור בניין העיר באבנים.
explanation.en: Brief separation is contrasted with great compassion and the bringing near of the exiles. The promise is given in the language of the Word of יְיָ and linked with the days of Noach and the floodwaters. Divine goodness and the covenant of peace are contrasted with passing mountains and hills, followed by an image of rebuilding the city in stone.

dayTitle.he: דברי החכמה אל הדוחים את עצתה
dayTitle.en: Wisdom’s words to those who reject her counsel

explanation.he: האזהרה מתארת ביאת בהלה, שבר וצרה אחרי דחיית הדעת והתוכחה. הדוחים אוכלים מפרי דרכיהם ומשביעים את עצמם מעצותיהם. הקטע מבחין בין סטיית הפתאים ובין טעות הכסילים, בלי לפרט אירוע היסטורי מסוים.
explanation.en: The warning describes terror, ruin, and distress after the rejection of knowledge and rebuke. Those who reject counsel eat the fruit of their own ways and are filled with their own counsels. The passage distinguishes the turning away of the simple from the error of fools, without identifying a particular historical event.

dayTitle.he: בקשה על החטאים, בניין המקדש והוראה
dayTitle.en: Prayer concerning sins, rebuilding the sanctuary, and teaching

explanation.he: בתרגום מתוארים בקשה על החטאים ובניין המקדש שחולל בעוונות. ההוראה וההקשבה לדברים נקשרות לריבוי שלום ולסליחה. התפילה נענית ומתקבלת עוד לפני פתיחת הפה; בסיום מתוארים מסירת תקיפי העמים לטבח והיעדר מי שיפתח את פיו כנגדו.
explanation.en: The Targum describes prayer concerning sins and the rebuilding of a sanctuary profaned through wrongdoing. Teaching and heeding the words are linked with increased peace and forgiveness. Prayer is answered and accepted even before the mouth is opened; the closing images describe the mighty ones of the peoples being handed over for slaughter and the absence of anyone opening his mouth against him.

dayTitle.he: קירוב הגלויות, טיהור השארית וחלק בביזה
dayTitle.en: Bringing the exiles near, purifying the remnant, and a share in spoil

explanation.he: התרגום מתאר את קירוב הגלויות ואת הסרת שלטון העמים מארץ ישראל. הוא מדבר על טיהור שארית העם ועל ראיית מלכות המשיח, ריבוי בנים ובנות והצלחה לעושי התורה. התיאור מסתיים בחלק בביזה, בבקשה על חטאים ובסליחה למורדים בזכותו.
explanation.en: The Targum describes bringing the exiles near and removing the rule of the peoples from the land of Israel. It speaks of purifying the remnant, seeing the Messiah's kingship, increase of sons and daughters, and success for those who practice Torah. The account ends with a share in spoil, prayer concerning sins, and forgiveness for rebels on his account.

dayTitle.en: Seeking wisdom and guarding the paths of judgment

explanation.he: החכמה נדרשת ככסף וכמטמונים, וידיעה מתוארת כמציאה מלפני אלהים. הדעת והבינה באות מפיו, ונזכרת העזרה להולכים בלא מום. שמירת דרכי המשפט ודרכי הצדיקים מסיימת את הקטע.
explanation.en: Wisdom is sought like silver and stored-up treasure, and knowledge is described as being found from before God. Knowledge and understanding come from His mouth, and help is given to those who walk without blemish. The passage ends with guarding the paths of judgment and the righteous.

dayTitle.he: הדרכים העקומות והאזהרה מן האשה הזרה
dayTitle.en: Crooked paths and the warning concerning the strange woman

explanation.he: הקטע ממשיך את תיאור הדרכים העקומות ומזהיר מן האשה הזרה ומדבריה המתוקים. האשה מתוארת כמי ששכחה את ברית אלהים. ביתה נמצא בעומק המוות, והאזהרה מסיימת שהנכנסים אינם חוזרים בשלום ואינם משיגים את דרכי החיים. זהו תיאורה של האשה המסוימת שבקטע, ולא קביעה על כל אשה מארץ אחרת.
explanation.en: The passage continues the description of crooked paths and warns concerning the strange woman and her sweet words. She is described as forgetting the covenant of God. Her house is in the depth of death, and the warning ends by saying that those who enter do not return in peace or attain the paths of life. This describes the particular woman in the passage, not every woman from another land.
